23.sentence: Course of illness:        **** is a 14 month old female[FP19].

24.sentence: She was born at 36 weeks 3 days via repeat C Section.

25.sentence: She was diagnosed with Persistent Left ******** Vena Cava to Coronary Sinus;  Aorta without narrowing with tiny Patent Ductus Arteriosus[FP20].

26.sentence: She was discharged at 3 days old.

27.sentence: She was recommended for outpatient follow up with peds cardiology within one month of discharge.

28.sentence: However, she was not seen until almost 6 months of age.

29.sentence: She was doing well, and was not recommended for any additional cardiology follow-up unless she became symptomatic.

30.sentence: She reportedly had a fairly normal first year of life, with the exception of frequent emesis and poor growth.

31.sentence: She presented to OSH the day prior to admission here with fatigue, decreased feeding, decreased urination, and increased work of breathing.

32.sentence: She was also found to be anemic, and was given a large PRBC transfusion.

33.sentence: She was then transferred to our hospital for further management.

34.sentence: She was found to have severely dilated LV with severely depressed function.

35.sentence: She was also intubated due to worsening respiratory status and increased lactic acidosis.

36.sentence: She is now being evaluated for possible escalation of care to include ECMO, VAD, and transplant.

44.sentence: They report that **** was on a liquid medication for her heart rate, but they cannot remember what it was.

78.sentence: Adherence:  There are several concerns for adherence documented[FP37].  **** had a prenatal ultrasound that was concerning for dilated coronary sinus with slight RV predominance, suspicion for persistent LSVC and need to rule out COA.

79.sentence: She was referred to pediatric fetal cardiology several times for further evaluation of this.

81.sentence: In addition, there is concern that mom did not keep her own medical appointments and care during the pregnancy, and her diabetes was 'poorly controlled'[FP39].

82.sentence: This led to an admission for DKA.

83.sentence: After **** was born, she was referred for follow up with pediatric cardiology at 1 month of life.

84.sentence: However, she did not follow up until age 5 months[FP40].

86.sentence: She was at 0.06 % on the growth chart for weight on the day of admission.

89.sentence: She was primarily receiving breast milk, as she was not really tolerating solid foods.

90.sentence: Parents report that they are a little nervous at the thought of having to administer medications on a strict schedule[FP42].

91.sentence: However, they believe they will be able to do so.

96.sentence: She states she cannot have any other children, and cannot fathom life without **** in it.
